Dispersive blow-up for a coupled Schrödinger-fifth order KdV system

Eddye Bustamante Affiliation: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Medellín Email: eabusta0@unal.edu.co    José Jiménez Urrea Affiliation: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Medellín Email: jmjimene@unal.edu.co    Jorge Mejía Affiliation: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Medellín Email: jemejia@unal.edu.co
Abstract

In this work we establish a dispersive blow-up result for the initial value problem (IVP) for the coupled Schrödinger-fifth order Korteweg-de Vries system

i​ut+∂x2u=αuv+γ|u|2u,x∈ℝ,t∈ℝ,∂tv+∂x5v+∂xv2=ϵ∂x|u|2,x∈ℝ,t∈ℝ,u⁡(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x).}\displaystyle\left.\begin{array}[]{rl}iu_{t}+\partial_{x}^{2}u&\hskip-5.69054pt=\alpha uv+\gamma|u|^{2}u,\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in\mathbb{R},\\ \partial_{t}v+\partial_{x}^{5}v+\partial_{x}v^{2}&\hskip-5.69054pt=\epsilon\partial_{x}|u|^{2},\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in\mathbb{R},\\ u(x,0)&\hskip-5.69054pt=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x).\end{array}\right\}

To achieve this, we prove a local well-posedness result in Bourgain spaces of the type Xs+β,b×Ys,bX^{s+\beta,b}\times Y^{s,b}, along with a regularity property for the nonlinear part of the IVP solutions. This property enables the construction of initial data that leads to the dispersive blow-up phenomenon.

1 Introduction

11footnotetext: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 35Q53

In this article we consider the initial value problem (IVP) for the coupled Schrödinger-fifth order Korteweg-de Vries system on the line:

i​ut+∂x2u=αuv+γ|u|2u,x∈ℝ,t∈ℝ,∂tv+∂x5v+∂xv2=ϵ∂x|u|2,x∈ℝ,t∈ℝ,u⁡(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),}\displaystyle\left.\begin{array}[]{rl}iu_{t}+\partial_{x}^{2}u&\hskip-5.69054pt=\alpha uv+\gamma|u|^{2}u,\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in\mathbb{R},\\ \partial_{t}v+\partial_{x}^{5}v+\partial_{x}v^{2}&\hskip-5.69054pt=\epsilon\partial_{x}|u|^{2},\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in\mathbb{R},\\ u(x,0)&\hskip-5.69054pt=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\end{array}\right\}

where u=u⁡(x,t)∈ℂu=u(x,t)\in\mathbb{C}, v=v⁡(x,t)∈ℝv=v(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}, and α,γ,ϵ\alpha,\gamma,\epsilon are real constants.

The system (1) is a particular case of the Schrödinger-Kawahara system

i​ut+∂x2u=α​u​v+γ​|u|2​u,∂tv+β​∂x3v−δ​∂x5v+v​∂xv=ϵ​∂x|u|2,u⁡(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),}\displaystyle\left.\begin{array}[]{rl}iu_{t}+\partial_{x}^{2}u&\hskip-5.69054pt=\alpha uv+\gamma|u|^{2}u,\\ \partial_{t}v+\beta\partial_{x}^{3}v-\delta\partial_{x}^{5}v+v\partial_{x}v&\hskip-5.69054pt=\epsilon\partial_{x}|u|^{2},\\ u(x,0)&\hskip-5.69054pt=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\end{array}\right\}

where α,β,γ,δ\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta are real constants.

The system (1) was studied by Shin in [14]. It describes phenomena related to the interaction between short uu and long vv waves. Shin proves in this article that the IVP (1) is locally well-posed when the initial data u0u_{0} and v0v_{0} are taken in the Sobolev spaces Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) and Hk​(ℝ)H^{k}(\mathbb{R}), respectively, with s≥0s\geq 0, k≥−2k\geq-2 and s−4≤k<min⁡{8​s+1,s+2}s-4\leq k<\min\{8s+1,s+2\}, provided δ≠0\delta\neq 0. This result is achieved by combining technics developed by Guo and Wan in [8] and Kato in [9] for the Schrödinger-Korteweg-de Vries system. Furthermore, Shin establishes the global well-posedness of the IVP (1) when (u0,v0)∈L2​(ℝ)×L2​(ℝ)(u_{0},v_{0})\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})\times L^{2}(\mathbb{R}), under the condition δ≠0\delta\neq 0, by adapting the method employed by Colliander, Holmer and Tzirakis in [5] for the Zakharov and Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger systems in low regularity settings.

Although in our work we consider initial data that meet the hypotheses of Shin’s article, we again establish the local well-posedness of the IVP (1) in the context of specific Bourgain spaces, which allow us, through their norms, to measure the regularity gains associated with the nonlinear terms of the system.

Let us remember that, formally, a pair (u,v)(u,v) is a solution of the IVP (1) if and only if

In a precise manner, we prove the following result.

Theorem 1.1.

(Local well posedness of the IVP (1)). Let s≥0s\geq 0, 920<b<12\frac{9}{20}<b<\frac{1}{2}, 12<β<52​b−58\frac{1}{2}<\beta<\frac{5}{2}b-\frac{5}{8} and let u0∈Hs+β​(ℝx)u_{0}\in H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}_{x}) and v0∈Hs​(ℝx)v_{0}\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}_{x}). There exist T∈(0,12]T\in(0,\frac{1}{2}] and a unique

(u,v)∈(Xs+β,b∩C⁡(ℝt,Hs+β​(ℝx)))×(Ys,b∩C⁡(ℝt,Hs​(ℝx)))(u,v)\in(X^{s+\beta,b}\cap C(\mathbb{R}_{t};H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}_{x})))\times(Y^{s,b}\cap C(\mathbb{R}_{t};H^{s}(\mathbb{R}_{x})))

solution of the integral equations (1.13) and (1.14).

(The restriction of uu and vv to ℝ×[0,T]\mathbb{R}\times[0,T] is a local solution in time of the IVP (1)).

We would like to point out that the result obtained in Theorem 1.1 does not include negative indices. However, the functional framework in which it is set is suitable for our purposes in this article. In contrast, Shin’s result in [14] covers a much broader range of low-regularity spaces, for which it is necessary to use Besov-type spaces.

In this work, our main focus is on studying dispersive blow-up for the coupled system (1). From a physical perspective, this phenomenon reflects the formation of singularities caused by the interaction between short and long waves. For coupled systems of dispersive-type equations, the first result in this direction was obtained by Linares and Palacios in [10], where they consider a nonlinear Schrödinger-Korteweg de Vries system and prove that the nonlinear part of the solution of the system is smoother than the solution. In this manner the existence of dispersive blow-up for the system is provided by the linear dispersive solution. Our next result is also to prove that the nonlinear part of the solution of the IVP (1) is smoother than the solution.

Some similar results have been obtained for nonlinear dispersive equations such as the KdV equation (see [2]), the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (see [4]) and the Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation (see [11]). For related results, see also [13].

In [10], in order to prove this result, it is required, in addition to the smoothing properties of the groups associated with the linear Schrödinger and linear KdV equations, the use of the persistence property of the solution of the system in weighted Sobolev spaces.

For the system considered in our work, the use of Bourgain spaces and the regularity gain of the nonlinear terms of the system, measured through its norms in these spaces, are sufficient to prove that the nonlinear part of the solution is smoother than the solution. This approach, inspired by the work of Erdogan and Tzirakis [7], avoids the use of the persistence property of the solution of the system in weighted Sobolev spaces, and we think that it simplifies the reasoning significantly. The precise formulation of this result is as follows.

Theorem 1.2.

(Regularity gain of the nonlinear part of the solution). Let s≥0s\geq 0, 920<b<12\frac{9}{20}<b<\frac{1}{2} and 12<β<52​b−58\frac{1}{2}<\beta<\frac{5}{2}b-\frac{5}{8}. Let u0∈Hs+β​(ℝx)u_{0}\in H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}_{x}) and v0∈Hs​(ℝx)v_{0}\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}_{x}). Let us take a¯\overline{a} and aa such that

0≤a¯≤52​b−58−β​ and ​0≤a≤5​β−94.0\leq\overline{a}\leq\frac{5}{2}b-\frac{5}{8}-\beta\text{ and }0\leq a\leq 5\beta-\frac{9}{4}.

On the other hand, let T∈(0,12]T\in(0,\frac{1}{2}] and

(u,v)∈(Xs+β,b∩C⁡(ℝt,Hs+β​(ℝx)))×(Ys,b∩C⁡(ℝt,Hs​(ℝx))),(u,v)\in(X^{s+\beta,b}\cap C(\mathbb{R}_{t};H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}_{x})))\times(Y^{s,b}\cap C(\mathbb{R}_{t};H^{s}(\mathbb{R}_{x}))),

as in Theorem 1.1. Then

Our main goal in this paper is to establish a dispersive blow-up result for the IVP (1). In [2], Bona and Saut prove the existence of dispersive blow-up for the generalized KdV equation. The idea behind the Bona and Saut proof is to observe that the nonlinear part of the solution is smoother than the solution. In this manner it is sufficient to choose initial data that gives rise to the formation of singularities for the solution of the linearized IVP. Following this idea, in [12] and [10], the authors establish the dispersive blow-up for the generalized KdV equation and the Schrödinger-KdV system, respectively.

Using the regularity gain in Theorem 1.2 and by imitating the procedure in [10] for the construction of the initial data, we prove the following result on dispersive blow-up for the IVP (1).

Theorem 1.3.

(Dispersive blow-up). There exist initial data u0∈C∞​(ℝ)∩H2−​(ℝ)∩L∞​(ℝ)u_{0}\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})\cap H^{2^{-}}(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}) and v0∈C∞​(ℝ)∩H32−​(ℝ)∩L∞​(ℝ)v_{0}\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})\cap H^{\frac{3}{2}^{-}}(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}), and t∗∈(0,T]t^{*}\in(0,T] ([0,T][0,T] is the time interval in which the local solution (u,v)(u,v) of the IVP (1) with initial data u0u_{0} and v0v_{0}, is defined) such that

  • (i)

    u⁡(t∗)∉C1,12+ϵ​(ℝ)u(t^{*})\notin C^{1,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}(\mathbb{R}) for some ϵ∈(0,12)\epsilon\in(0,\frac{1}{2}) and

  • (ii)

    v⁡(t∗)∉C1​(ℝ)v(t^{*})\notin C^{1}(\mathbb{R}).

(Let us recall that Hs−​(ℝ)=⋂s′<sHs′​(ℝ)H^{s^{-}}(\mathbb{R})=\bigcap_{s^{\prime}<s}H^{s^{\prime}}(\mathbb{R}). The definition of the space C1,α​(ℝ)C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) is given in Section 5).

Our work is organized as follows. In Section 2 we present the linear and nonlinear estimates needed for proving the local-well posedness of IVP (1). It is important to point out the gain of regularity in the nonlinear estimates. In Section 3 we prove the local-well posedness of IVP (1) (proof of Theorem 1.1). In Section 4 we establish the gain of regularity of the nonlinear part of the solution of IVP (1) (proof of Theorem 1.2). Finally, in Section 5, we construct the initial data u0u_{0} and v0v_{0} that gives rise to de dispersive blow-up (proof of Theorem 1.3).

Throughout the paper the letter CC will denote diverse constants, which may change from line to line, and whose dependence on certain parameters is clearly established in all cases.

Taking into account that for s>0s>0 and 0≤α≤min⁡{s−12,1}0\leq\alpha\leq\min\{s-\frac{1}{2},1\}, Hs​(ℝ)↪C0,α​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\hookrightarrow C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}), we deduce that u1​(t)∈C0,α​(ℝ)u_{1}(t)\in C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) for 0≤α≤10\leq\alpha\leq 1 and u1′​(t)∈C0,α​(ℝ)u_{1}^{\prime}(t)\in C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) for 0≤α≤min⁡{s1−1−12,1}0\leq\alpha\leq\min\{s_{1}-1-\frac{1}{2},1\}.

Since min⁡{s1−1−12,1}≥min⁡{1+116−12,1}=12+116\min\{s_{1}-1-\frac{1}{2},1\}\geq\min\{1+\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{2},1\}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{16}, we conclude that u1​(t)∈C1,α​(ℝ)u_{1}(t)\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) for 0≤α≤12+1160\leq\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{16} for every t∈[0,T]t\in[0,T].

On the other hand, since s~1>32+18\tilde{s}_{1}>\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{8}, we have that v1​(t)∈C1​(ℝ)v_{1}(t)\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}) for every t∈[0,T]t\in[0,T]. Let us take θ>0\theta>0 such that t∗:=14​θ∈[0,T]t^{*}:=\frac{1}{4\theta}\in[0,T]. Hence, from (5.7), taking into account that U⁡(t∗)​u0∉C1,12+ϵ​(ℝ)U(t^{*})u_{0}\notin C^{1,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}(\mathbb{R}) for ϵ∈(0,12)\epsilon\in(0,\frac{1}{2}) and u1​(t∗)∈C1,α​(ℝ)u_{1}(t^{*})\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) for 0≤α≤12+1160\leq\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{16}, we conclude that u⁡(t∗)∉C1,α​(ℝ)u(t^{*})\notin C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}) for 0≤α≤12+1160\leq\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{16}.

In this way, there exist ϵ∈(0,12)\epsilon\in(0,\frac{1}{2}) such that u⁡(t∗)∉C1,12+ϵu(t^{*})\notin C^{1,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}.

Finally, from (5.8), observing that V⁡(t∗)​v0∉C1​(ℝ)V(t^{*})v_{0}\notin C^{1}(\mathbb{R}) and that v1​(t∗)∈C1​(ℝ)v_{1}(t^{*})\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R}), we conclude that v⁡(t∗)∉C1​(ℝ)v(t^{*})\notin C^{1}(\mathbb{R}). This completes the proof of Theorem 1.3.∎
